author: AI Editorial Team (Esi)
key_learning_objective: Recognize the key monitoring parameter for spironolactone.
question_stem: A client with heart failure is taking spironolactone. Which laboratory value should the nurse monitor most closely?

rationales.A: Correct. Spironolactone is a potassium-sparing diuretic; it retains potassium and can cause hyperkalemia, so potassium must be monitored closely and salt substitutes avoided.
rationales.B: Sodium is relevant to fluid status but is not the priority electrolyte risk with this drug.
rationales.C: Spironolactone does not primarily affect the WBC count.
rationales.D: Calcium is not the key value affected by spironolactone.

key_takeaway: Spironolactone spares potassium - watch for HYPERkalemia (opposite of furosemide).
nclex_test_taking_tip: Contrast paired drugs: furosemide lowers K+, spironolactone raises it.
memory_trick: spironolactONE spares potassium - it climbs UP.
clinical_pearls: Teach avoidance of salt substitutes and high-K+ foods in excess.
Hyperkalemia risk rises when combined with ACE inhibitors/ARBs.
